competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

postmortems.what_worked: March 2027 SOFR implied fell from the 4.58 entry to the 4.24 exit, so the view that the forward was stretched high and would normalize lower was right, and the close kept the result instead of retargeting cash at 3.92.
postmortems.what_failed: The realized paper increment was only 250 dollars after about 47 days, so a 34bp favorable move stayed a small book outcome at conviction 56.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The thesis held. Implied normalized from 4.58 to 4.24, and the live invalidation did not force the exit. The close was taken after the stretch had been given back.
postmortems.expression_assessment: Long March SOFR was the right instrument for that policy-path fade. At 4.27, with cash at 3.92, the same long is no longer a fresh extreme and should not be reopened from memory of the 4.58 entry.
postmortems.timing_assessment: The hold of about 47 days and the exit on 6 Nov at 4.24 matched the normalization window. Staying for a full gap close to cash would have been a different trade.
postmortems.sizing_assessment: Conviction 56 correctly kept the expression modest. A 250 dollar increment on a realized normalization is a bounded outcome of that conviction, not evidence the position should have been sized up after the move was known.

causal.original_belief: March 2027 implied at 4.58 was stretched above a plausible lower path and would mean-revert unless another 25bp was delivered into the December window with March holding at or above the prior June mid, or hotter US labor and inflation re-widened the oil tail.
causal.observed_reality: Implied fell from 4.58 to 4.24 by 6 Nov, the position was closed for a 250 dollar paper increment after about 47 days, and the current screen shows cash SOFR at 3.92 with March at 4.27.
causal.assumptions_right: The elevated March implied was vulnerable to normalization, the decline occurred, and the stated hawkish invalidation did not have to print for the exit at 4.24 to be the right close of that stretch.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: How far the gap to cash would close was underweighted. Implied stalled near 4.24, still well above cash at 3.92, so the full premium to cash was never the right target, and a modest conviction correctly treated the labor and oil tails as a reason to keep size small.
causal.causal_divergence: The forward did the thing the thesis asked, a 34bp decline from 4.58 to 4.24, while the book recorded only 250 dollars because the expression was sized for a 56 conviction rather than for a full move to cash.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same 4.58 entry and the same invalidation, the sound path was still to hold the long while the forward stayed stretched and to exit once it had fallen to 4.24. Raising size after the decline was known would have used information that was not available at entry.
causal.future_implication: A completed normalization is not a reason to reload the same March long at 4.27, and a later rates fade needs a fresh stretch versus cash and the curve rather than the memory of the 4.58 entry.

postmortems.no_new_lesson: The process was sound. The stretch was identified, the invalidation was specific, the forward normalized, and the exit followed that normalization. The 250 dollar increment is the bounded variance of a 56-conviction expression held for about 47 days, not a defect in the anchor or the exit rule. The same rule is what keeps March from being reopened now that the entry extreme is gone.
